title: Community-label workflow (label-community job): skip bot and internal-association PRs in job-level `if`, not in the shell step
answers: Why does the community-label action still start a runner for bot PRs or maintainer PRs?
Where is the bot and MEMBER/COLLABORATOR/OWNER exclusion for community labeling handled?
How do I add another cheap skip condition to a GitHub Actions job without paying for a runner?
Why does the Databricks profile and commit-email check still run in a shell step?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/community-label.yml:label-community job. Decides which pull_request events get the community label. Covers bot-authored PRs, internal PRs by author_association, and the external-author path that calls `gh api users/$AUTHOR` and checks company/email for Databricks affiliation before labeling.
Rule: Put eligibility checks that only read event context (user.type, author_association, repository) in the job-level `if:` so ineligible PRs are skipped before runner allocation. Keep only checks that need an API call or a lookup (profile company/email, commit-email affiliation) in the run script. Do not duplicate a job-level gate as a shell `exit 0` guard.
Symptom: Bot and internal PRs used to allocate an ubuntu-slim runner, run the step, and exit 0 after the shell guard fired, wasting runner time on every such PR.
Constraints: Job-level `if:` can only use event fields and expressions, not API results, so it cannot replace the profile lookup. The author_association list is written as fromJSON('["MEMBER","COLLABORATOR","OWNER"]') inside `contains`. Applies to this workflow; other workflows may still use shell guards.
applies: Applies to .github/workflows/community-label.yml; general pattern for any GitHub Actions job that filters pull_request events.
says: Automated community labeling wastes runner minutes on internal team pull requests.
Stop allocating cloud build machines for bot pull requests that skip labeling.
Pull request triage automation spends compute credits running jobs for repository maintainers.
Skip automated labeling jobs before provisioning runners when the author is a collaborator.
search: In .github/workflows/community-label.yml:label-community, filter out bot authors (user.type) and internal contributors using job-level `if:` with contains(fromJSON('["MEMBER","COLLABORATOR","OWNER"]'), github.event.pull_request.author_association) before runner allocation. This avoids provisioning an ubuntu-slim runner only to exit 0 in a shell script guard. API calls like `gh api users/$AUTHOR` that inspect Databricks company or commit-email affiliation remain inside the step script because job-level conditions cannot evaluate external API results. This rule applies specifically to community-label.yml as a pattern for filtering pull_request workflows.
